newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Quintiles sees major Asian revenue boost.
newsitem.headline: Quintiles sees major Asian revenue boost.

text.p: U.S. medical research contract company Quintiles Transnational Corp is aiming to boost its Asia-Pacific business to around 25 percent of revenue over the next decade from the current level of less than 10 percent, company executive Michael Bassett said on Friday.

Speaking at the opening of Quintile's regional data processing centre in Adelaide, Bassett told Reuters the company's current revenue in Asia totalled around US$30 million, with about US$6 million generated in Australia.

Quintiles' chief executive officer, contract research organisation, Ludo Reynders said the company sought to achieve substantial organic growth topped up by opportuninistic but strategic acquisitions which met geographic, service, or therapeutic specialisation needs for the company.
There were, he said, a lot of corporate opportunities in Australia.

"Some of them are of interest to us ... certainly in Australia there are a few people who seem to have done the right thing at the right time and we might well have a word with them at the time when it is most appropriate," he said.

Bassett, Quintile's Asia Pacific vice-president, said the main opportunities for regional growth in the short-term were in contract research, with an increasing investment in contract selling over the next few years.

The company's third business tier, health economics services, would remain relatively marginal but was well-placed to take up opportunities in assisting emerging Asian economies to maximise their public health spending, he said.
"I would say (that by 2005) we would want the Asia Pacific area to be around 25 percent of Quintile's business," he said.
But Reynders declined to be more specific.
Quintiles in February acquired the Sydney-based DCCG Consulting Group, establishing its first contract sales operation for the region.
